questions.question: Rani Karnaa was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi (1996) for her contribution to_
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rani Karnaa borne in 1939 in **Hyderabad, Sindh** (now in Pakistan).
 
• Rani Karnaa was a distinguished Indian classical dancer known for her expertise in Kathak.
 
• She trained under legendary **gurus such as Nrityacharya Narayan Prasad, Pandit Sunder Prasad, and Pandit Birju Maharaj.**
 
• Rani Karnaa was renowned for blending the **Jaipur and Lucknow gharanas**, creating a unique and aesthetically rich style.
 
• She received numerous accolades, including the **Padma Shri in 2014** and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1996.

**Kathak:**

 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of** Indian classical dance**, originating from the traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• The dance form evolved during the **Bhakti movement**, incorporating stories of Hindu gods, particularly Krishna.
 
• It further developed under the patronage of **Mughal emperors, integrating Persian elements.**
 
• Kathak has **three main gharanas (schools)** - **Jaipur, Lucknow, and Banaras**.
 
• The Jaipur gharana emphasizes intricate footwork, while the Lucknow gharana focuses on facial expressions and graceful hand movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Odissi: **Originating from Odisha, this dance form is known for its fluid movements and **sculpturesque poses.** Notable exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Sonal Mansingh.
 
• **Kathakali:** A classical dance-drama from Kerala, **characterized by elaborate costumes** and makeup. Famous artists include Kalamandalam Gopi and Margi Vijayakumar.
 
• **Kuchipudi:** Hailing from Andhra Pradesh, this dance form is known for its graceful movements and **strong narrative.** Renowned dancers include Vempati Chinna Satyam and Yamini Krishnamurthy.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The President shall, notwithstanding the expiration of his/her term, continue to hold office until his successor enters upon his/her office?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 56**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 56 of the Indian Constitution deals with the term of** office of the President.**
 
• It states that the President shall hold office for **a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.**
 
• It includes a provision that the President shall, **notwithstanding the expiration of his term**, continue to hold office until his successor enters upon his office.
 
• This ensures a smooth transition and avoids any vacancy in the office of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Article 61:** Deals with the procedure for** impeachment of the President** for violation of the Constitution.

**Article 58: **Specifies the **qualifications for election** as President.

**Article 50:** Relates to the **separation of judiciary from the executive** in the public services of the state.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the chairman of the National Commission for Backward classes in December 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Hansraj Gangaram Ahir**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hansraj Gangaram Ahir was appointed as the chairman of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) in December 2022.
 
• He is a **former Union Minister of State for Home Affairs.**
 
• Ahir has been a prominent leader from Maharashtra and has served as a Member of Parliament.

**National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)**

 
• **102nd Constitution Amendment Act, 2018** granted constitutional status to the NCBC.
 
• **Article 338B** provides the NCBC with the authority to investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the socially and educationally backward classes under the Constitution or under any other law.
 
• **Constitution (127th Amendment) bill, 2021:** This amendment allows states and union territories to prepare and maintain their own lists of SEBCs.
 
• **Article 342A:** Initially, this article empowered only the President to specify SEBCs in consultation with the Governor of the concerned state. The 2021 amendment restored the states’ authority in this matter.
 
• **Mandal Commission** established in 1979, it recommended reservations for OBCs in government jobs and educational institutions, leading to the implementation of** 27% reservation** for OBCs in 1990.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** **Development Process of NCBC**

 
• The** first backward classes commission** was established under the chairmanship of **Kaka Kalelkar** to identify the socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• The commission submitted its report in 1955, but its recommendations were not implemented.
 
• Second Backward Classes Commission (1979) (Mandal Commission):Headed by **B.P. Mandal,** this commission was tasked with identifying the **criteria for defining** socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• The Mandal Commission’s report, submitted in 1980,** recommended a 27% reservation** for OBCs in government jobs and educational institutions. These recommendations were implemented in 1990.
 
• The Supreme Court, in the landmark **Indra Sawhney & Others v. Union of India case**, directed the establishment of a permanent body to examine and recommend the inclusion and exclusion of various Backward Classes. This led to the creation of the NCBC.
 
• The NCBC was constituted as a **statutory body under National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993 **to address the issues of backward classes.

**Structure of NCBC**

 
• **Chairperson:** Appointed by the President
 
• Vice-Chairperson
 
• **Three Other Members: **These members are appointed by the President and include individuals with special knowledge or experience in matters related to backward classes.

questions.question: With which sport is the Burdwan Trophy associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weightlifting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Weightlifting:

__
 
• Weightlifting is a sport in which athletes compete in lifting a barbell loaded with weight plates from the ground to overhead.
 
• Athletes compete in two specific ways of lifting the barbell overhead.
 
• These are:
 
 
• the snatch
 
• the clean and jerk.
 
 

Explanation:__

__
 
• The snatch is a wide-grip lift, in which the weighted barbell is lifted overhead in one motion.
 
• The clean and jerk is a combination lift, in which the weight is first taken from the ground to the front of the shoulders (the clean), and then from the shoulders to overhead (the jerk).
 
• The clean and press, wherein a clean was followed by an overhead press, was formerly also a competition lift but was discontinued due to difficulties in judging proper form.
 
• To keep competing the player has to increase at least 5 kg of weight between two attempts if the first one is successful.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Few rules(officiating):

 
• During the competition, the snatch event takes place first, followed by a short intermission, and then the clean and jerk event.
 
• There are two side judges and one head referee who together provide a "successful" or "failed" result for each attempt based on their observation of the lift within the governing body's rules and regulations.
 
• Two successes are required for any attempt to pass.
 
• Usually, the judges' and referee's results are registered via a lighting system with a white light indicating a "successful" lift and a red light indicating a "failed" lift.

• A satellite is a moon, planet, or machine that orbits a planet or star.
 
• For example, Earth is a satellite because it orbits the sun.
 
• Likewise, the moon is a satellite because it orbits Earth.
 
• Usually, the word "satellite" refers to a machine that is launched into space and moves around Earth or another body in space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Koderma Gaya Hazaribagh belt is known for the production of which of the following minerals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mica**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Mica: 

 
• Mica (waste and scrap) is largely produced by the states of Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar, and Jharkhand.
 
• In Jharkhand, Koderma is the leading producer of Mica. It is located in the Hazaribagh belt of Jharkhand. Jharkhand is quite rich in minerals.
 
• The Koderma district and the Lokai-Indarwa area cover the southern part of the Great Mica-Belt of Jharkhand and Bihar.
 
• The mica belt stretches from Gurpa in Gaya district in the west through Nawada, Koderma, Hazaribagh, Giridih in Jharkhand and Jamui as well as Bhagalpur district of the Bihar state in the east.
 
• Its maximum width is about 40 km in the Koderma-Hazaribagh-Nawada area.

​Bauxite: 

 
• States with the largest bauxite reserves in India: Odisha (50%), Maharashtra (10%), Gujarat (6.6%), Chhattisgarh (6%).
 
• In Maharashtra, there are bauxite reserves in the districts of Kolhapur, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, Raigad, and Thane.
 
• In Odisha the reserves are in the district of Kalahandi, Koraput, Sundargarh, Bolangir and Sambalpur.
 
• In Jharkhand the reserves are in the district of Dumka, Lohardaga, Munger, Palamu, Ranchi.

Coal: 

 
• West Bengal most important reserve and mining field is the Raniganj.
 
• It covers around 443.50 km2 in the Bardhman and Birbhum districts of West Bengal.
 
• Raniganj coalfield is the second largest coalfield in the country (in terms of reserves).

​Copper: 

 
• ​The major copper mines are the Khetri copper belt in Rajasthan, Singhbhum copper belt in Jharkhand and Malanjkhand copper belt in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘All doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision shall be final’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 71.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 71 of the Indian Constitution states that all doubts and **disputes arising out of or in connection with the election** of a** President or Vice-President **shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court.
 
• This provision ensures that the **Supreme Court has the final authority in resolving any issues related to the election **of these high offices, maintaining the integrity of the electoral process.
 
• The mechanism provided in **Article 71 helps prevent any political ambiguity regarding the election** outcomes, thereby strengthening public trust in the electoral system.
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India is the **apex court** of the Indian judicial system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 69** deals with the Oath or affirmation by the Vice-President.
 
• **Article 70** discusses the circumstances under which the President can continue in office despite the vacancy.
 
• **Article 68** Time of holding election to fill vacancy in the office of Vice President and the term of office of person elected to fill casual vacancy
 
• **Article 66** deals with the election of the Vice-President.
 
• **Article 54** of the Constitution of India is about the** election** of the President of India.
 
• **Article 55** of the Indian Constitution outlines the **manner of election **of the President of India.

questions.question: What is the growth rate of population of India as per census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1764.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, India's population growth rate was approximately **17.64% from 2001 to 2011**, which translates to a growth rate of 0.1764 when expressed in decimal form.
 
• The total population of India as per the 2011 Census was around **1.21 billion.**
 
• The Census 2011 revealed that India had a **sex ratio of 940 females for every 1,000 males**, indicating ongoing gender imbalances.
 
• The overall literacy rate in India increased to **74.04%**, with **male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%**, highlighting ongoing efforts in education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Census is the most credible** source of information on Demography** (Population characteristics), Economic Activity, Literacy and Education, Housing Household Amenities, Urbanisation, Fertility and Mortality, etc. 
 
• The 2011 census of India was the **seventh census** after India gained independence and the** 15th** in a series of continuous censuses since 1872:
 
• Census was introduced in India during the era of** Lord Mayo in the year 1872**. It came into force in 1881.
 
• This census was conducted under the guidance of **Mr. C. Chandramouli.**
 
• The slogan of Census 2011 was** ‘Our Census, Our future’.**
 
• The population of the nation as per the provisional figures of **Census 2011 was 1210.19 million** of which 623.7 million (51.54%) were males and 586.46 million (48.46%) were females.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state** in India its population is more than the population of Brazil.

questions.question: Which of the following was discovered by GN Ramachandran?

options.text: Fluid mosaic model of a cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Triple helical structure of collagen.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **G.N. Ramachandran** is renowned for his significant contributions to biochemistry, particularly for elucidating the triple helical structure of collagen.
 
• His work established that collagen, a key structural protein in connective tissues, consists of** three polypeptide chain**s that form a right-handed triple helix.
 
• The discovery of collagen's structure has** implications for medicine**, particularly in understanding diseases related to connective tissues.
 
• Ramachandran's work has earned him recognition as a **pioneer in structural biology,** influencing subsequent research in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model of a Cell:**

 
 
• Proposed by **Singer and Nicolson in 1972**, this model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic and flexible structure with a mosaic of various proteins floating in or on the fluid lipid bilayer.
 
• It highlights the importance of membrane proteins in functions such as signaling, transport, and maintaining cell shape.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• The plasma membrane is the** outer boundary of the cell **that separates its interior from the external environment.
 
• Composed of a lipid bilayer with embedded proteins, it regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, playing a crucial role in cell communication and homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Bodies:**
 
 
• Also known as the **Golgi apparatus**, these organelles are involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• **Discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898**, the Golgi apparatus is essential for processing molecules synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.question: The Vienna Convention is related to ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protection of ozone layer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Vienna Convention**, formally known as the Vienna Convention for the** Protection of the Ozone Layer**, was adopted in **1985** to address the depletion of the ozone layer.
 
• The convention is a **legally binding agreement** that aims to promote international cooperation to protect the ozone layer. It encourages countries to: 
 
 
• Exchange information and conduct research on the ozone layer 
 
• Adopt laws and regulations to protect the ozone layer 
 
• Develop controls for ozone layer development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montreal Protocol:**

 
 
• Adopted in** 1987**, this protocol aims to **phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances,** such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
 
• It is considered one of the most successful environmental treaties, leading to significant recovery of the ozone layer.
 
 
 
• **Kyoto Protocol:**
 
 
• Adopted in **1997**, this international agreement commits its parties to **reduce greenhouse gas emissions**, based on the premise that global warming exists and human-made CO2 emissions have caused it.
 
• The protocol emphasizes binding commitments for developed countries to mitigate climate change.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• Adopted in **2015,** this landmark accord aims to** limit global warming** to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.
 
• It encourages countries to set their emission reduction targets and report on their progress.
 
 
 
• **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**
 
 
• Established in** 1992**, this convention aims to conserve biological diversity, promote sustainable use of its components, and ensure fair sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of preserving ecosystems and species.
 
 
 
• **UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):**
 
 
• Adopted in **1992**, this treaty sets the framework for international efforts to combat climate change, with periodic Conferences of the Parties (COP) to assess progress and set binding commitments.

questions.question: In 2023, Government of India has proposed to set up ‘Central Processing Centre’ for faster response to organisations through centralised handling of various forms filed with field offices under the _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Companies Act.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Companies Act of** 2013 **states that companies must maintain **documents electronically.**
 
• It also mandates that board meetings be given **at least 7 days' notice.**
 
• The Act defines the **duties of directors, key managerial personnel, and promoters**. 
 
• The Companies Act, 2013 was** preceded by the Companies Act, 1956.**
 
• Due to changes in the national and international economic environment and to facilitate expansion and growth of our economy, the Central Government decided to replace the Companies Act, 1956 with the new legislation.
 
• The Companies Act 1956 was an Act of the Parliament of India, enacted in 1956, which enabled **companies to be formed by registration**, and set out the responsibilities of companies, their directors, and secretaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partnership Act**

 
 
• The Partnership Act of **1932 **states that a partnership is created by agreement, not status.
 
• It also states that a** minor can't be a partner** in a firm, but they can benefit from it. 
 
 
 
• **Contract Act**
 
 
• The Indian Contract Act of **1872** covers topics such as **communication, acceptance, and revocation of proposals.**
 
• It also defines terms like **consent, free consent, coercion, undue influence, fraud, and misrepresentation.** 
 
 
 
• **Sale of Goods Act**
 
 
• The Sale of Goods Act of** 1930 **states that the** intention of the parties to a contract** determines whether the contract passes property in the goods from the buyer to the seller.
 
• It also states that** sellers can sue for the price of goods** in case of breach, even if the goods are still in their possession.

questions.question: Which of the following Indo-Greek kings was mentioned in the Buddhist text Milindapanho as Milinda?

__
 
• **Menander I** ruled during the 2nd century BCE and is one of the most notable **Indo-Greek kings.**
 
• He is prominently mentioned in the **Buddhist text Milindapanho, **where he is referred to as Milinda.
 
• Known for his discussions with Buddhist monks, particularly on philosophical topics.
 
• His reign represents **a blend of Greek and Indian cultures**, promoting the spread of Buddhism.
 
• Menander I expanded his kingdom significantly, **covering parts of modern-day India and Pakistan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demetrius I**

 
 
• Ruled in the **3rd century BCE**.
 
• Known for expanding the Indo-Greek kingdom.
 
• Notable for **military campaigns in northern India.**
 
 
 
• **Antiochus II**
 
 
• A less prominent Indo-Greek king.
 
• Ruled after Demetrius I, with limited historical significance in Buddhist texts.
 
 
 
• **Strato II**
 
 
• Succeeded Menander I.
 
• Known for a **peaceful reign** but lacks significant references in Buddhist literature.

questions.question: Select the correct statement.

options.text: The pyramid of energy is always upright.
The pyramid of biomass is always inverted.
The pyramid of mass is always upright.
The pyramid of number is always upright.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The pyramid of energy is always upright**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A pyramid of biomass is a graphical representation that shows the population at each level of the food chain.
 
• Producers occupy the base with the highest biomass.
 
• The relationship between numbers, biomass, energy, or bio productivity of an ecosystem can be represented by a pyramid known as the ecological pyramid.
 
• The trophic level is the place that a living organism occupies in a food chain.
 
• In a biomass pyramid, producers are at the base, followed by herbivores and then carnivores at the top.
 
• The pyramid of biomass shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
 
• 10 percent of the energy gets transferred to the next trophic level and the rest is either utilized for metabolic processes or excreted out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carnivores that eat herbivores are called secondary consumers.
 
• A separate trophic level, the decomposers or transformers, consists of organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead organisms and waste materials into nutrients usable by the producers.
 
• Primary consumers make up the second trophic level. They are also called herbivores.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and select the correct option.

A. Directive Principles of State Policy consists of all the ideals which the state should follow and keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws for the country.

B. It can be enforced by the Judiciary.

C. They can be suspended during a national emergency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Directive Principles of State Policy

 
• Articles 36-51 under Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deal with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• They are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.
 
• It refers to the ideals that the State should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws. e.g. the Government should try to ensure equal pay for equal work for men and women etc. 
 
• Non-justiciable nature on recommendations of Tej Bahadur committee Report
 
• Positive Connotation – Establishes social and economic democracy.
 
• Promote the concept of a Welfare State and Inclusive Growth.
 
• Precursors of Panchayat Raj Institution (Art. 40- Village Panchayat)
 
• Fundamental in governance and apply in policy makings – Art. 37
 
• Novel features and Soul of the constitution – B.R Ambedkar
 
• DPSP is the Conscience of the constitution – Granville Austin
 
• Constitutional instructions to – Legislature, executive, and administration of the state.
 
• Enabling in nature – Enables government for a comprehensive program of social and economic justice, unlike FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS.
 
• Non-justiciable, Non-self-executory, non-enforceable by a court of law.
 
• Government can implement provisions of DPSP by legislative actions.

Significance of DPSP

 
• Helps courts as Guiding Light in determining and examining the constitutional validity of acts/rules/regulations.
 
• Symbolizes the idea of a welfare state and amplifies social and economic justice as entailed in the Preamble.
 
• They impose a moral obligation on the state authorities for their application, however, public opinion is the real force behind them.
 
• Serves as moral precepts for – Legislature, executive, and administration of state
 
• They serve as a Common Minimum Programme for every government irrespective of their manifestos and political ideologies.
 
• The Directives are the life-giving provisions of the Constitution. They constitute the stuff of the Constitution and its philosophy of social justice. – L. M Singhvi. Hence, Option 1 is correct.
 
• Directives lay down that the goal of Indian polity is ‘economic democracy’ as distinguished from ‘political democracy’ (Fundamental rights) – R. Ambedkar
 
• Supplements and complements Fundamental Rights (Part III).
 
• Serves as benchmarks and yardstick for people to gauge the performance of govt.
 
• DPSPs are intended to be a guide, friends, and philosophers of the ruling party in legislative and executive acts.
 
• Serves as an important tool for opposition parties to ensure accountability of the executive and exercise influence and control over the government.

questions.question: Which was the prominent architectural feature of the Indus Valley towns and cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Citadel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Indus Valley Civilisation:
 
 
• John Marshall was the first scholar to use the term ‘Indus Valley Civilisation’.
 
• The Indus Valley Civilisation belongs to the Protohistoric Period (Chalcolithic Age/Bronze Age).
 
• Dayaram Sahni first discovered Harappa Civilisation in 1921.
 
• R.D. Banerjee discovered Mohenjodaro or Mound of the Dead in 1922.
 
• Mohenjodaro–The largest site of Indus Valley Civilisation.
 
• Rakhigarhi–The largest Indian site of Indus Valley Civilisation.
 
• Common features of major cities: Systematic town planning on the lines of grid system; Use of burnt bricks in construction; Underground drainage system (giant water reservoirs in Dholavira); Fortified citadel (exception: Chanhudaro).

questions.question: Which of the following options is not related to the non-cooperation movement started by Mahatma Gandhi?

options.text: Signing of the resolution for Poorna Swaraj in Lahore

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Signing of the resolution for Poorna Swaraj in Lahore**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **non-cooperation movement** was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 to resist British rule in India through non-violent means.
 
• The movement included the **boycott of foreign goods**, which aimed at promoting Indian-made products and crippling British economic interests in India.
 
• The **distribution of spinning wheels** was encouraged to promote self-reliance and the use of khadi (hand-spun cloth).
 
• **Picketing at liquor shops** was part of the movement to oppose British-imposed taxes on liquor and to promote temperance.
 
• **Signing of the resolution for Poorna Swaraj in Lahore** is not related to the non-cooperation movement. It was part of a different phase in India's struggle for independence, specifically the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in 1929 where the demand for complete independence was formalized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The non-cooperation movement was a significant phase in the Indian independence struggle, involving millions of Indians who withdrew their cooperation from the British government.
 
• It was characterized by the use of non-violent methods such as non-payment of taxes, surrender of titles, and boycott of British educational institutions and law courts.
 
• The movement was eventually called off by Gandhi in 1922 following the Chauri Chaura incident, where a violent clash led to the death of police officers.
 
• The **Lahore Session** in 1929 was a turning point as it marked the formal adoption of the goal of Poorna Swaraj or complete independence from British rule.

questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was one of the co-founders of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) which got established in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagat Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA):

 
 
• Hindustan Republic Association at a historic meeting in the ruins of Ferozshah Kotla in Delhi was converted into Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in September 1928.
 
• Under the leadership of Chandra Shekhar Azad, the name of HRA was changed to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
 
• The participants included Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Bhagwaticharan Vohra from Punjab and Bejoy Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma and Jaidev Kapur from the United Provinces.
 
• The HSRA decided to work under a collective leadership and adopted socialism as its official goal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bhagat Singh Founded Naujawan Bharat Sabha in March 1926.
 
• The objective of this organisation was to encourage revolution against British rule by rallying the peasants and workers.
 
• Bhagat Singh established contact with Sohan Singh Josh and through him ‘the worker and peasants party’ which brought out the monthly magazine Kirti in Punjabi.
 
• Bhagat Singh:
 
 
• Bhagat Singh was born on September 1907, in Lyallpur western Punjab, India ( Now in Pakistan) 
 
• In 1923, he joined National College in Lahore founded by Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
• Bhagat Singh was deeply affected by the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• In 1928, He established the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) along with Chandrashekhar and others.
 
• Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt, on April 8th,1929, threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly.
 
• On 23 March 1931 Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were Hanged by the British Government.
 
• At that time his age was a little more than 23 years.

questions.question: On 11 May 2023, the Uttarakhand Chief Minister launched the ‘Smart School Smart Block Programme’ in the Goralchod auditorium in the state’s ________ district.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champawat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• On May 11, 2023, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami launched the “Smart School Smart Block Programme” in the Goralchod auditorium in the state's Champawat district. 
 
• The program's goals include: Making teaching more systematic and easy, Developing teachers' capabilities, and Making learning joyful for students. 

 The program was initially implemented in 137 schools of Champawat Block, where 274 teachers were trained to improve the learning outcomes of 5484 children. 

 
• After 100 days of successful implementation, the program was extended to the Khrishu block of Pauri district.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option:

i. Marginal Worker is a person who works for less than 183 days (or six months) in a year.

ii. Main Worker is a person who works for atleast 300 days (or ten months) in a year.

options.text: Both i and ii are correct.
Both i and ii are incorrect.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only i is correct.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Workers were mainly classified as main and marginal workers based on their work.
 
• Those workers who had worked for the major part of the year were termed as main workers.
 
 
• The major part of the year meant six months (183 days) or more.
 
 
 
• Those who had not worked for the major part of the year ( i.e. those who had worked for less than 6 months or less than 183 days in a year) were termed as marginal workers.
 
• In 2001 the percentage of main workers of the total people was 30.2%.
 
• The percentage of marginal workers reflects a less developing economy and poverty.
 
• Most of the marginal workers are the land-less agricultural laborers in rural areas.
